statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the maximum total tastiness over all purchase plans (S, C) such that S ⊆ {0,...,n-1}, C ⊆ S, |C| <= maxCoupons, and the total price sum_{i in S\C} price[i] + sum_{i in C} floor(price[i]/2) is at most maxAmount; the tastiness of such a plan is sum_{i in S} tastiness[i]. Equivalently, r = max { sum_{i in S} tastiness[i] | S ⊆ {0,...,n-1}, C ⊆ S, |C| <= maxCoupons, sum_{i in S\C} price[i] + sum_{i in C} floor(price[i]/2) <= maxAmount }. The empty plan (S = C = ∅) is allowed and gives tastiness 0.
preconditions: n = len(price) = len(tastiness); 1 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= price[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= tastiness[i] <= 1000; 0 <= maxAmount <= 1000; 0 <= maxCoupons <= 5. All values are 64-bit integers; price[i]/2 denotes integer division rounding down (floor).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (i.e., it does not fail, panic, or overflow).
preconditions: n = len(price) = len(tastiness); 1 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= price[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= tastiness[i] <= 1000; 0 <= maxAmount <= 1000; 0 <= maxCoupons <= 5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= 0.
preconditions: n = len(price) = len(tastiness); 1 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= price[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= tastiness[i] <= 1000; 0 <= maxAmount <= 1000; 0 <= maxCoupons <= 5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= sum_{i=0}^{n-1} tastiness[i].
preconditions: n = len(price) = len(tastiness); 1 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= price[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= tastiness[i] <= 1000; 0 <= maxAmount <= 1000; 0 <= maxCoupons <= 5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist sets S and C with C ⊆ S ⊆ {0,...,n-1} such that |C| <= maxCoupons, sum_{i in S\C} price[i] + sum_{i in C} floor(price[i]/2) <= maxAmount, and sum_{i in S} tastiness[i] = r.
preconditions: n = len(price) = len(tastiness); 1 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= price[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= tastiness[i] <= 1000; 0 <= maxAmount <= 1000; 0 <= maxCoupons <= 5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every pair of sets S, C with C ⊆ S ⊆ {0,...,n-1}, |C| <= maxCoupons, and sum_{i in S\C} price[i] + sum_{i in C} floor(price[i]/2) <= maxAmount, we have sum_{i in S} tastiness[i] <= r.
preconditions: n = len(price) = len(tastiness); 1 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= price[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= tastiness[i] <= 1000; 0 <= maxAmount <= 1000; 0 <= maxCoupons <= 5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a subset S ⊆ {0,...,n-1} such that r = sum_{i in S} tastiness[i].
preconditions: n = len(price) = len(tastiness); 1 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= price[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= tastiness[i] <= 1000; 0 <= maxAmount <= 1000; 0 <= maxCoupons <= 5.

statement: Whenever the function returns r on (price, tastiness, maxAmount, maxCoupons) and returns r' on (price', tastiness', maxAmount, maxCoupons), we have r = r'.
preconditions: n = len(price) = len(tastiness); 1 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= price[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= tastiness[i] <= 1000; 0 <= maxAmount <= 1000; 0 <= maxCoupons <= 5. Let π be any permutation of {0,...,n-1}, and define slices price' and tastiness' of length n by price'[i] = price[π(i)] and tastiness'[i] = tastiness[π(i)] for 0 <= i < n.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r equals the maximum over all subsets S ⊆ {0,...,n-1} with sum_{i in S} floor(price[i]/2) <= maxAmount of sum_{i in S} tastiness[i].
preconditions: n = len(price) = len(tastiness); 1 <= n <= 100; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= price[i] <= 1000 and 0 <= tastiness[i] <= 1000; 0 <= maxAmount <= 1000; maxCoupons >= n.
